original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Exact paid-factor counts in the right-vector alphabet I + u y^T (u in R^n, y in K^n) with free GL_n(K) maps: cost <= 1 for every n and every K-algebra R, an exact two-factor criterion at n = 2 for every R, and its consequences over M_m(K), local algebras and F2[S3]. Answers open questions 2 and 3 of #4265 at n = 2, and open question 1 at n = 2 for local algebras.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a larger or nonabelian register model escapes the scoped three-register obstruction. This package answers narrower open questions left by #4243 and #4265 about the exact cost in the right-vector alphabet over nonabelian and non-field coefficient algebras.
bottleneck_link: Side result in a formal alphabet. It decides which targets cost two right-vector factors at n = 2; it prices no native frame or supplier, and kappa is unchanged.
stop_rule: Prove the two-factor criterion, check it against exhaustive search on every target of small algebras, settle the F2[S3] lift, then stop.
evidence: PROOF.md proves Theorems A-D. verify.py --stage main checks the criterion against breadth-first search on all 77,824 targets over five algebras (agreement everywhere; 12 + 72 cost-3 targets over UT2(F2) and M2(F2); 12 unreachable targets over F2[x,y]/(x,y)^2), the local statement, the M_m(K) rank form over M2(F2), and an explicit cost-3 target over F2[S3]. --stage s3 counts 120,060 criterion failures among all 2^24 targets over F2[S3].
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Is every reachable target at n = 2 reachable with three factors, for every K-algebra?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Together with Theorem B it would give the exact cost at n = 2. Search finds maximum reachable cost 3 on all five algebras here.
open_questions.first_step: Characterise the three-factor set (G x I)[[A, 0], [B, 1]][[1, C], [0, D]][[E, 0], [F, 1]](H x I) as Theorem B does for two factors.
open_questions.blocked_by: Only the two-factor set is characterised here.

open_questions.question: What is the cost <= k criterion for n >= 3?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The right-ideal condition of Theorem B should generalise to a flag condition on block-triangular factorizations.
open_questions.first_step: With y_1..y_k a basis, products of k factors are block column operations; write the n = 3, k = 2 condition and test it by search over F2[C2] or UT2(F2).

open_questions.question: Is delta exact for invertible targets over every commutative K-algebra at n = 2?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Theorem D proves it for local algebras; products such as F2 x F2 need one (G, H) that works in every factor at once.
open_questions.first_step: Prove the criterion for invertible M over a product of local algebras with residue field K, or find a counterexample by criterion counting over F3 x F3 x F3.
open_questions.blocked_by: Non-local commutative algebras are only checked on F2 x F2 and F2[C3] (here and in #4265).
